chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid Shabab al-Sayrafi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said:

When death came upon Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), he called al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام). He said to al-Abbas, “O uncle of Muhammad, will you take the inheritance of Muhammad, settle his debt, and fulfill his promises?” He replied, “O Rasul Allah, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, I am an old man with many dependents and little wealth; who can bear your burden while you outdo the wind in generosity?” He said: then he (صلى الله عليه وآله) was silent for a little while, then said, “O Abbas, will you take the inheritance of Muhammad, fulfill his promises, and settle his debt?” He said, “May my father and mother be ransomed for you, I am an old man with many dependents and little wealth, and you outdo the wind.” He said, “Indeed, I shall give it to one who will take it with its due right.”

Then he said, “O Ali, O brother of Muhammad, will you fulfill the promises of Muhammad, settle his debt, and take possession of his inheritance?” He said, “Yes, may my father and mother be ransomed for you; that is upon me and belongs to me.” He said: then I looked at him until he removed his ring from his finger and said, “Wear this during my lifetime.” He said: then I looked at the ring when I placed it upon my finger, and from all that he left behind I wished for the ring. Then he called out, “O Bilal, bring me the helmet, the armor, the banner, the shirt, Dhu al-Faqar, al-Sahab, the cloak, the al-abraqah, and the staff.” He said: by Allah, I had not seen it except at that very hour—meaning al-abraqah—then a piece was brought that nearly dazzled the eyes, and it was from the brocades of al-Jannah.
Then he said, “O Ali, Jibra'il came to me with it and said: O Muhammad, place it in the ring of the armor and fasten yourself with it in the place of the belt.”

Then he called for two Arabian sandals together, one of them patched and the other unpatched; and for two shirts: the shirt in which he was taken on the Night Journey, and the shirt in which he went out on the Day of Uhud; and for the three caps: the cap of travel, the cap of the two Eids and Fridays, and a cap that he used to wear while sitting with his companions.

Then he said, “O Bilal, bring me the two mules al-Shahba' and al-Duldul, the two she-camels al-Adba' and al-Qaswa', the two horses—al-Janah, which used to be kept at the door of the mosque for the needs of Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), such that he would send a man for a matter and he would ride it and hasten upon it in the need of Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)—and Hayzum, the one about which he used to say, ‘Advance, Hayzum,’ and the donkey Ufayr.” Then he said, “Take possession of them during my lifetime.” Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) mentioned that the first of the animals to die was Ufayr: at the moment Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was taken, it broke its rein, then went running until it came to the well of Banu Khatmah at Quba', and threw itself into it, and that became its grave.

And it is narrated that Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) said: that donkey spoke to Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and said, “May my father and mother be ransomed for you. My father narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, that he was with Nuh in the Ark. Nuh came to him, wiped over his croup, then said: from the loins of this donkey there shall come a donkey that the master of the Prophets and their seal will ride. So praise belongs to Allah who made me that donkey.”

key_terms.اقْبِضْهَا: take possession of them during my lifetime
key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the Ark of Nuh mentioned in the closing report
key_terms.الْأَبْرَقَةِ: a shining article described as being from the brocades of al-Jannah
key_terms.تُرَاثَ: inheritance or legacy left behind by the Prophet
key_terms.خَاتَمَهُ: the Prophet’s ring given to Imam Ali
key_terms.دَيْنَهُ: the debts that were to be repaid on his behalf
key_terms.ذِي الْفَقَارِ: the famed sword Dhu al-Faqar among the Prophet’s entrusted items
key_terms.عِدَاتِهِ: his promises and commitments that were to be fulfilled

ai.seo_question: How did Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) entrust his inheritance, debts, and personal effects to Imam Ali (عليه السلام) at the end of his life?
ai.summary: This narration describes the final moments of Rasul Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) as he entrusted his debts, promises, personal effects, weapons, and mounts to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (عليه السلام). It highlights the transfer of the Prophet’s belongings and responsibilities to Imam Ali (عليه السلام), and includes mention of sacred objects and a report concerning the donkey Ufayr.
